title: Discovering Invariant and Changing Mechanisms from Data

problem.claim: Causal mechanisms may vary across domains because of population-specific differences, data-collection context, or intervention.

gap.claim: Existing work has emphasized invariant causal mechanisms, leaving a need to discover both invariant and changing mechanisms from data.

contributions.claim: The paper extends the algorithmic model for causation to represent mechanism changes and instantiates the extension using Minimum Description Length.
For a continuous variable Y observed across contexts C, the method identifies variables X as causal when the regression functions from X to Y have succinct descriptions in all contexts.
The resulting method, VARIO, is designed to find invariant variable sets, reveal mechanism changes, and discover causal networks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: In empirical evaluations, VARIO finds invariant variable sets.
In empirical evaluations, VARIO reveals mechanism changes.
The method discovers causal networks on real-world data that provide insight into signaling pathways in human immune cells.

narrative_sequence.summary: Causal mechanisms can be invariant or vary across domains for several contextual reasons.
The paper proposes extending the algorithmic model for causation to mechanism changes using Minimum Description Length.
Variables are treated as causal when their regression functions to a continuous outcome have succinct descriptions across all contexts.
Empirical evaluations report that VARIO identifies invariant sets, exposes mechanism changes, and discovers causal networks, including in human immune-cell data.

source_observation.claim: The method evaluates whether regression functions have succinct descriptions across multiple contexts.

interpretation.claim: Cross-context description length can serve as a criterion for distinguishing stable causal structure from context-dependent mechanism changes.

application.claim: When modeling data from heterogeneous domains, assess both invariance and mechanism change instead of assuming that causal mechanisms remain fixed.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when succinct descriptions reliably identify causality or how the criterion behaves under particular data limitations.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the optimization procedure or implementation details of VARIO.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or evaluation conditions.
The abstract does not characterize the assumptions required for causal identification.
